# Excess mortality during heatwaves

Excess mortality is the difference between the deaths observed during a heatwave
and the deaths a baseline model expected from the same weeks in ordinary years.
The baseline is the whole argument: a model fitted on the previous five summers
gives a different number than one fitted on the previous fifteen.

## Baseline modelling and age stratification

The baseline is fitted per city on daily temperature and mortality, with a
spline for season and a term for humidity, and the excess is the sum of the
positive residuals over the episode. Age stratification matters more than the
total: the excess concentrates above seventy five years and in dwellings without
cooling, and a city average hides both.

Attribution to climate change is a separate step: it compares the episode with
and without the observed warming, and only that comparison supports the causal
claim.
